1	# WP-003: Create Test Database Seeding Script
     2	
     3	## Description
     4	
     5	Create the standalone seeding script `tests/seed-test-db.php` and register the `composer seed-tests` command, providing the infrastructure that the refactored bootstrap will reference when system users are missing.
     6	
     7	## Scope
     8	
     9	- `tests/seed-test-db.php` (new file)
    10	- `composer.json` (`scripts` section)
    11	
    12	## Dependencies
    13	
    14	- WP-002 (Refactor TestSuiteBootstrap — provides `seedSystemUsers()`)
    15	
    16	## Acceptance Criteria
    17	
    18	1. `tests/seed-test-db.php` exists and contains `declare(strict_types=1)`, defines `TESTS_ROOT` and `APP_TESTS_RUNNING`, requires `tests/bootstrap.php`, and calls `TestSuiteBootstrap::seedSystemUsers()`.
    19	2. `composer.json` contains a `seed-tests` script entry that runs `php tests/seed-test-db.php`.
    20	3. Running `composer seed-tests` executes without error when the test database is accessible and the `seedSystemUsers()` method exists.
    21	
    22	## Active Pipeline Stages
    23	
    24	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    25	
    26	## Implementation Guidance
    27	
    28	**New file:** `tests/seed-test-db.php`
    29	```php
    30	<?php
    31	/**
    32	 * Seeds system users into the test database.
    33	 * Invoked via: composer seed-tests
    34	 *
    35	 * @package Application
    36	 * @subpackage Tests
    37	 */
    38	
    39	declare(strict_types=1);
    40	
    41	use Application\Bootstrap\Screen\TestSuiteBootstrap;
    42	
    43	$testsRoot = __DIR__;
    44	
    45	define('TESTS_ROOT', $testsRoot);
    46	define('APP_TESTS_RUNNING', true);
    47	
    48	require_once __DIR__ . '/bootstrap.php';
    49	
    50	TestSuiteBootstrap::seedSystemUsers();
    51	
    52	echo "Test database seeded successfully.\n";
    53	```
    54	
    55	**Modified file:** `composer.json` — add to `scripts` section:
    56	```json
    57	"seed-tests": "php tests/seed-test-db.php"
    58	```

msg.content: 1 2 3 # Application Framework 4 5 All-in-one PHP framework and UI layer for building web and intranet 6 applications. 7 8 ## Introduction 9 10 The framework is designed to be a solid foundation for custom-built web 11 applications. The integrated functionality helps to focus on the application 12 logic, while being able to create the necessary administration screens, 13 APIs and more with minimal effort. 14 15 Note that it is not a CMS: it is exclusively a tool for building custom 16 applications. Supporting features are available out of the box, like the 17 notepad or image library, but anything your application needs to do must 18 be implemented by you. 19 20 One of the core functionalities of the framework is to provide an extensive 21 ecology of classes for accessing custom data stored in the database. 22 This includes complex filtering capabilities as well as a versioning 23 system with record state tracking (draft, published, etc.). 24 25 ## Features overview 26 27 - PHP helper classes for UI elements 28 - Form building system - every screen is a form 29 - Rule-based application environment detection 30 - Advanced database-stored data handling tools 31 - Class-based extensible templating system 32 - Localization system for UI translation 33 - News central (release notes, etc.) 34 - Event handling system 35 - Image media library and UI 36 - Tagging system and UI 37 - Versioning system with state tracking 38 - Disposables system for automated garbage collection 39 - API response caching (file-based, opt-in via Interface + Trait; TTL and manual strategies) 40 - SSO via CAS 41 - Interface Translations: English, German, French 42 - Build-time module documentation generators (Modules Overview, Keyword Glossary) 43 - Own ecology of supporting libraries 44 45 ## Requirements 46 47 - PHP 7.4 or higher (fully PHP 8 compatible) 48 - [Composer](https://getcomposer.org) 49 - MariaDB or MySQL database with InnoDB support 50 - Webserver 51 52 ## Installation 53 54 The framework can be installed as a regular Composer dependency. 55 However, the required application skeleton of folders and files 56 can currently only be generated dynamically using the 57 [Framework Manager][], which is currently still a private project. 58 59 Documentation on how to set up an application using the framework 60 is still in progress. In the meantime, the example application can 61 be used as a reference (see [Example application](#example-application)). 62 63 ## Example application 64 65 The framework includes a sample application which is used as a reference for 66 available features, best practices, and testing. It can also be used as 67 the basis for a new application. 68 69 You will find it in the `tests/application` folder. 70 71 **Installation** 72 73 1. Import the SQL file `tests/sql/testsuite.sql` into a database. 74 2. Open the folder `tests/application/config`. 75 3. Copy `test-db-config.dist.php` to `test-db-config.php`. 76 4. Copy `test-ui-config.dist.php` to `test-ui-config.php`. 77 5. Edit the settings in both files. 78 6. Access the `tests/application` folder via the webserver. 79 80 ## Composer commands 81 82 These are custom Composer commands that are available 83 when developing locally. 84 85 ### Build 86 87 The build step generates module documentation artefacts from `module-context.yaml` 88 files discovered throughout the codebase, updates the CTX `generated-at.txt` 89 timestamp, regenerates the API method index, and rebuilds offline event listeners. 90 91 ```bash 92 composer build 93 ``` 94 95 For the full development build (includes module glossary and keyword index): 96 97 ```bash 98 composer build-dev 99 ```

100	
   101	### Clear caches
   102	
   103	Clears all caches used by the framework, including the dynamic
   104	class cache.
   105	
   106	```bash
   107	composer clear-caches
   108	```
   109	
   110	## Build-Time Documentation Generators
   111	
   112	The `Application\Composer` namespace provides build-time utilities that generate
   113	two Markdown documentation artefacts automatically on every `composer build`:
   114	
   115	- **Modules Overview** (`docs/agents/project-manifest/modules-overview.md`) — a
   116	  Markdown table of all modules, their source paths, context doc locations, and
   117	  inter-module dependencies. Discovered from `module-context.yaml` files.
   118	- **Keyword Glossary** (`docs/agents/project-manifest/module-glossary.md`) — a
   119	  Markdown glossary mapping opaque domain terms to the modules that define them.
   120	  Application modules can contribute custom sections via the `DecorateGlossaryEvent`
   121	  offline event.
   122	
   123	To register a module for discovery, add a `module-context.yaml` next to its classes:
   124	
   125	```yaml
   126	moduleMetaData:
   127	  id: "my-module"
   128	  label: "My Module"
   129	  description: "What this module does."
   130	  keywords:
   131	    - "Widget (the core UI component)"
   132	```
   133	
   134	See [`src/classes/Application/Composer/README.md`](src/classes/Application/Composer/README.md)
   135	for full API documentation and the offline-event integration guide.
   136	
   137	## CTX Integration
   138	
   139	The project uses CTX to generate context files for AI-assisted development,
   140	and to provide an MCP server for integration with IDEs like PHPStorm to 
   141	access the framework's AI tools.
   142	
   143	### Related commands
   144	
   145	#### Start the MCP Server
   146	
   147	```bash
   148	ctx server
   149	```
   150	
   151	#### Generate all files
   152	
   153	```bash
   154	ctx generate 
   155	```
   156	
   157	#### Server information
   158	
   159	This fetches a JSON-lines list of configurations and tools available 
   160	in the server.
   161	
   162	```bash
   163	(echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"test-client","version":"1.0.0"}}}'; \
   164	 echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}'; \
   165	 echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}') | ctx server -c context.yaml
   166	```
   167	
   168	## Documentation
   169	
   170	The framework's documentation is available locally by pointing a browser to 
   171	the `docs` folder, and online in the separate [Framework Documentation][]
   172	package. 
   173	
   174	> It is ideally viewed through the framework's documentation screen, as there
   175	> are some features that are only available there (like code samples that are
   176	> included dynamically). 
   177	
   178	### Vendor Package
   179	
   180	For convenience, a copy of the documentation is automatically checked out into 
   181	the vendor folder during the Composer install process.
   182	
   183	It can be found at [mistralys/application-framework-docs](/vendor/mistralys/application-framework-docs/README.md).
   184	
   185	## History
   186	
   187	The framework has its origins in several projects where the same development
   188	paradigms were used and refined over time. In 2013, it started to crystallize
   189	into a recognizable entity, and in 2015, it was officially split off into its
   190	own project.
   191	
   192	It was migrated to Github in february 2021, and modernizing the code has been
   193	ongoing ever since. As a result, the current state of the code is a mix of
   194	namespaced and non-namespaced code, with the goal of eventually moving to a
   195	fully namespaced codebase.
   196	
   197	[Framework Manager]: https://github.com/Mistralys/appframework-manager
   198	[Framework Documentation]: https://github.com/Mistralys/application-framework-docs

1	<?php
     2	/**
     3	 * Seeds system users into the test database.
     4	 * Invoked via: composer seed-tests
     5	 *
     6	 * ## Constant ordering constraint
     7	 *
     8	 * This script intentionally uses `define()` (rather than `const`) for
     9	 * TESTS_ROOT and APP_TESTS_RUNNING so that both constants are defined
    10	 * *before* `tests/bootstrap.php` is required.  The bootstrap file
    11	 * contains `const TESTS_ROOT = __DIR__` at file scope; because `const`
    12	 * declarations are evaluated at compile time and cannot be conditionally
    13	 * guarded, PHP would emit an E_WARNING ("Constant TESTS_ROOT already
    14	 * defined") if this script were to use `const` instead.  Using `define()`
    15	 * here keeps the first definition (from this script) in place and avoids
    16	 * the compile-time conflict.
    17	 *
    18	 * Note: the E_WARNING from bootstrap.php's unconditional `const TESTS_ROOT`
    19	 * is still emitted during a normal `composer seed-tests` run.  This is a
    20	 * pre-existing issue in bootstrap.php and is tracked as technical debt
    21	 * (see WP-003 pipeline comments).
    22	 *
    23	 * @package Application
    24	 * @subpackage Tests
    25	 */
    26	
    27	declare(strict_types=1);
    28	
    29	use Application\Bootstrap\Screen\TestSuiteBootstrap;
    30	
    31	$testsRoot = __DIR__;
    32	
    33	define('TESTS_ROOT', $testsRoot);
    34	define('APP_TESTS_RUNNING', true);
    35	
    36	require_once __DIR__ . '/bootstrap.php';
    37	
    38	try
    39	{
    40	    TestSuiteBootstrap::seedSystemUsers();
    41	}
    42	catch(\Throwable $e)
    43	{
    44	    echo 'Seeding failed: ' . $e->getMessage() . PHP_EOL;
    45	    exit(1);
    46	}
    47	
    48	echo "Test database seeded successfully.\n";
